title: Follow every joule.

study.title: Follow every joule.
study.summary: Inspect resonance, useful load power, copper loss and stored energy in a passive series circuit.

inputs.label: Drive frequency
inputs.meaning: Frequency of the assumed sinusoidal voltage source.

inputs.label: Source voltage
inputs.meaning: Root mean square voltage; equivalent heating measure for the sinusoidal source.

inputs.label: Load resistance
inputs.meaning: Useful resistive load; ideal constant resistance.

inputs.label: Series loss
inputs.meaning: Effective series dissipation in this teaching model.

assumptions: Ideal series circuit, inductance L=0.01 H (henry), capacitance C=0.0001 F (farad), periodic steady state.
Finite energy window 0.025 s; capacitor may be initially charged. Source, load, losses and stored-energy change are all counted.
setup: Begin with the virtual model; keep source, load and stored energy as separate channels.
For a future low-voltage test, obtain rated passive components and an isolated limited source through a qualified lab; component ratings and tolerances remain unspecified.
Measure time-aligned voltage and current across every energy port, including meter supplies and grounds.
controls: Detune the source and substitute a known load.
Independently integrate signed source work and verify the complete energy identity.
study.falsifier: A nonzero residual beyond independently propagated uncertainty shows missing ports, phase/timing error or model failure, and does not establish free energy.
study.scope: Known passive RLC model applied here, not a new energy device or proof of a Tesla extraordinary claim.

metrics.label: Load power
metrics.meaning: Energy delivered to the useful resistance each second.

metrics.label: Copper loss
metrics.meaning: Energy dissipated by the series loss resistance each second.

metrics.label: Energy residual
metrics.meaning: Source work minus load energy, loss and stored-energy change over 0.025 s.

metrics.label: Resonance
metrics.meaning: Ideal reactance-cancellation frequency, not a new source of energy.

warnings: Periodic steady state can contain initially stored capacitor energy; do not omit it from a finite-window budget.

equations.meaning: Z is complex impedance in ohms; i is the imaginary unit, pi is the circle constant; L in henry and C in farad.
Each W here is integrated work in joules, not watt; E is stored electric plus magnetic energy in joules.

glossary.Pa: Pascal, pressure equal to one newton per square metre.
glossary.K: Kelvin, the SI unit of temperature; temperature differences of 1K and 1°C have equal size.
glossary.ppm: Parts per million; a relative value multiplied by one million.
glossary.ppb: Parts per billion; a relative value multiplied by one billion.
glossary.RLC: A circuit containing resistance R in ohms, inductance L in henry and capacitance C in farad.
glossary.RMS: Root mean square, a waveform amplitude convention distinct from peak.
glossary.DAC: Digital-to-analog converter, the electronic stage that turns numeric samples into a voltage.
glossary.EEG: Electroencephalography, a measured scalp electrical signal; not simulated here.
glossary.SPL: Sound pressure level, an acoustic measurement requiring calibration.
glossary.GLB: Binary glTF, a 3D scene file format; this file contains illustrative geometry.
glossary.SVG: Scalable Vector Graphics, a vector drawing format.
glossary.OSF: Open Science Framework, the repository hosting the independently retrieved registration.
glossary.TOST: Two one-sided tests, an equivalence-testing method; its margin and uncertainty need a declared plan.
glossary.A: Position or condition A in the named protocol; not an ampere unless explicitly stated.
glossary.B: Position or condition B in the named protocol; not magnetic flux density unless explicitly stated.

sourceRecords.title: Haus & Melcher — Electromagnetic Fields and Energy §11.2, Poynting’s theorem
sourceRecords.readDepth: Official MIT textbook section: energy-conservation derivation, work density, stored energy and flux roles read.
sourceRecords.passage: The objective ... is to derive a statement of energy conservation from Maxwell’s equations.
sourceRecords.claim: EM resonance models must account for source work, stored energy, flux and dissipation; response amplitude alone does not show net energy generation.
sourceRecords.limitations: This is a foundational source, not a recent experimental paper. It does not establish any proposed device’s efficiency, passivity or safety.

sourceRecords.title: Tesla, US645576A — System of transmission of electrical energy (1900)
sourceRecords.readDepth: Patent description passages identifying driven oscillator, condenser and generator read; not a full claim construction or replication.
sourceRecords.passage: The source describes oscillatory condenser discharges through the primary and charging from a generator.
sourceRecords.claim: The historical proposal has an explicit energy source and tuned transmitter/receiver mechanism. A patent documents a proposal rather than tested efficiency.
sourceRecords.limitations: Historical high-voltage details are not apparatus instructions here. No free energy, antigravity or copper teleportation result follows from this patent.
